utterances.text: You emphasize that VetConnect is only one pathway to DVS.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Veterans can also reach you by phone, email, through resource centers, and at community events, and certainly that's important.

chapters.summary: Caban asks whether all veteran requests through any channel enter a single case management system. Orlando confirms the goal is for all cases to be in the VetConnect CRM powered by Combined Arms, with a data department tracking case open and closed status and staff assigned to coordinate referrals.
chapters.title: Caban Q&A: case management system and follow-up responsibility

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: If a veteran reaches out through any of those channels, is that request entered into a single case management system?

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: Thank you for that question.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: That is the goal, is for all clients and cases to be included in our CRM, which is VetConnect powered by Combined Arms.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: And as Commissioner stated, it predated her tenure in terms of the utilization of the system.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: But as we move forward, we're ensuring all staff are implementing these cases into the system.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So is someone assigned responsibility for following up?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And can DVS tell us whether that veteran actually received the help that they requested?

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: Thank you for that follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: So on the platform, with oversight from our data department that is actively tracking what those case open and closed status is, when someone does go on to VetConnect and they request a service, it does get assigned to a staff member who works in that unit.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: So it's not a case manager.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: Per se by definition, but they are responsible for the coordination of where that veteran will get referred to or what support is provided.

utterances.speaker: Yesenia Mata
utterances.text: And just to elaborate, this is what we've mentioned that with the new

utterances.speaker: Yesenia Mata
utterances.text: data department that has now been implemented with the agency along with the aftercare

utterances.speaker: Yesenia Mata
utterances.text: department, that's the goal to centralize this data and to be able to have that continuity of follow-up to ensure to know where veterans are going.

utterances.speaker: Yesenia Mata
utterances.text: To ensure that they did get the services that they needed.

chapters.summary: Caban asks what specific changes the city has made in response to findings that veterans die by suicide at twice the civilian rate, and whether measurable prevention goals exist. Orlando describes connecting at-risk veterans to services and building community before crisis.
chapters.title: Caban Q&A: suicide prevention goals and measurable outcomes

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Last question I'll ask in this round and then turn over to Chair Caban and my colleagues has to do with an issue that we've all touched upon, which is veterans who take their own life.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Commissioner, you testified that research covering 2012 through 2022

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: found that New York City veterans died by suicide at approximately twice the rate of the civilian population with particularly concerning disparities among younger veterans.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: What specific changes has the city made in response to those findings?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Have you established measurable suicide prevention goals?

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And how will we know whether the city's efforts are actually making a difference?

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: Thank you for that question.

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: And as we stated before of not being a clinical provider, what we are ensuring is that our

utterances.speaker: Nicole Orlando
utterances.text: follow-up with our veterans who may have been answering screeners that indicate they are at risk are being connected to additional services, as well as the emphasis on building that community and camaraderie to ensure that before we get to crisis, there is support for those veterans as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Family should not disappear from consideration simply because a form has no place for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I have a business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I have two.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I do business with the city and the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And just to let you...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Rikers Island, too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So when you think about this, we're out there, we're doing things, but we're basically invisible at this point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And.

chapters.summary: Nelson describes experiencing disrespect within an organization serving military families, including poor treatment of Gold Star, White Star, and Silver Star families and their children. She calls for stronger oversight, confidential complaint procedures, independent evaluation, and trauma-informed staff training for organizations receiving city funding.
chapters.title: Nelson testimony: accountability for organizations serving military families

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This is something that's real deep because we all experience it as a military connected community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: We also need to hold, and you guys spoke a little bit about this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: We also need to hold accountability in the organizations that serve us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I have personally experienced disrespect within an organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: With other Gold Star families, White Star, Silver Star families, even the children, with how they're being treated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I chose to leave.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I actually had a personal experience on 9-11 two years ago, but it just doesn't stop there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: There's so many of us that go through it, even in the military community that's working with us as military to help us with our paperwork, our benefits, our children's scholarships.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I went through that whole process, and I just helped a family member with their grandchild because they thought their grandchild wasn't going to go to college because of the service they was receiving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Horrible service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Veterans and military families deserve fair,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: understanding that they should be a protected demographics, meaning that dignity should never depend on someone's personal preference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I ask that council to strengthen oversight within its authority and encourage coordination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: with state and federal partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: That would include meaningful feedback from people, receiving services, accessible complaint procedures, independent evaluation and staff training, and respect trauma-informed communication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: No family should have to fight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: To be treated with dignity by an organization established to support them.

chapters.summary: Nelson praises more inclusive language in event announcements and publications that now reference military families alongside veterans. She raises the case of a fiancée of a killed service member who receives different benefits than surviving spouses, asking where non-traditional family members fit in housing assistance programs.
chapters.title: Nelson testimony: inclusive language and gaps in family recognition

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This is recognition more for military-connected families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I want to acknowledge that I am seeing meaningful changes in the language used in event announcements, articles, and public writings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I appreciate that more organizations are referring not only to veterans,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: but also to families, military families and military connected families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: If anybody know me, this is all I speak about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This inclusive language matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: When a communication says only veterans, it can unintentionally leave out military-connected families, including families whose veteran

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: loved one died from a health issue, a health condition, and families who did not personally serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Naming military-connected families, opening the doors for more people to step into these spaces, be recognized, and receive support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Now, I recently saw a public item identifying Gold Star families in connection with housing with the veterans also in a whole article, which was beautiful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Now, it speaks about housing assistance schedule to launch on October 1st.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: FYI, October 1st is the 20th year anniversary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: My late husband, Sergeant Mario, was killed in combat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So I am hitting 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Now, my question is around this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: For those that are not considered Gold Star families,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: For those that...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I met a young lady that is, she was a fiance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Her fiance was killed riding his motorcycle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: She will not receive the same benefits that I received.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: She received something totally different.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Now, does that include that particular demographics of a family?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Because you can't call a surviving spouse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So where does that include her?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And she has four children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I want to affirm that these efforts are being heard and are making a difference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I also have additional matters to raise in a future meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Honoring Adam.

chapters.summary: Nelson honors Anthony Passaro's son Adam, a combat veteran who died by suicide. She describes connecting Anthony to the Dwyer program and credits DVS, particularly former Commissioner Hendon, for helping her emerge from isolation to advocate for families.
chapters.title: Nelson testimony: honoring Adam Passaro and gratitude for Dwyer program

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Before I come to a complete close, I would like to recognize someone whose experience helped deepen my commitment to advocating for White Star families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And just to hear the commissioner and the DVS team speak about the Dwyer program, I was one of the organizations that was part of the Dwyer program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And when I met Anthony, I told him about the program and he would come and attend the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And this is another way that I was able to actually help him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So I personally am grateful for the Dwyer's program, just to let you know that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Anthony is here in memory of his son, Adam Passaro, a combat veteran who later worked for Homeland Security and died by suicide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Anthony has shared the grief his family continues to carry and the isolation he felt before finding connection and support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: His family's experience is one reason I continue raising this issue, including in conversations with former Commissioner James Hendon and in my testimony before this council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Today can hold both gratitude and grief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Recognition cannot bring Adam back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: But it can help ensure that his family

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: and other families living.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: With this loss, feel seen, remembered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And less alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: We also have a Gold Star mother.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: watching, although she will not be speaking today, I want to acknowledge her presence and the importance of making

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Participation accessible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Thank you for hearing us and for helping move this recognition forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I ask that we carry that commitment into accessible services, economic opportunities, and accountability.

chapters.summary: Nelson expresses frustration that her multiple requests to meet with Councilmember Areola's office about the White Star Family resolution went unanswered. She emphasizes this is about communication and inclusion, not blame, and asks for meaningful engagement with affected families.
chapters.title: Nelson testimony: communication concerns with Councilmember Areola's office

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I would like to say something before Anthony come on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I don't believe you guys have this copy, but.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I do believe in positive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I do believe in working together as a community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: But what I don't appreciate is lack of communication and poor communication or no communication or just disregarding someone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I know personally, I bring this to the table September 22nd of last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Like I said, I don't do this for myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I do this with all my heart.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And I work closely with these communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Once I learned that the resolution was being worked on, I made multiple requests to meet with Councilmember Areola's office, which I understood was handling the matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I did not receive a response to my emails, my phone calls, text messages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I had made clear that I was available and willing to contribute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I am here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Please reach out to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: When those requests went unanswered, I felt disregarded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I understand that council offices have many demands, but acknowledging those requests and making space for a conversation would have mattered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I brought this issue forward with a purpose to help ensure that White Star families could be heard and that their experiences would inform the work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Being done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: A roundtable or meeting with White Star families would have been a meaningful opportunity to hear their concerns directly and understand their needs as a whole.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: The families affected by this recognition deserves a voice in what comes next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This is not about assigning blame.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Please understand, this is all about peace and love.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: It is about communication, inclusion, and ensuring that the families connected to this work have an opportunity to be heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I remain grateful that the recognition for these families is moving forward, and I hope there can still be a meaningful engagement with the families affected by the resolution.

chapters.summary: Morano thanks Nelson for channeling grief into activism, asks about the Gold Star mother who couldn't attend, and offers to connect her with his office. Nelson confirms this is a broader problem affecting multiple families. Morano proposes a committee roundtable and asks for three priority issues.
chapters.title: Morano Q&A with Nelson: Gold Star mother accessibility and roundtable priorities

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: First of all, thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Before we get to Anthony, you know, on behalf of the committee and the council and all Staten Islanders, we've all experienced grief and trauma.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I don't know that many of us have experienced the kind of grief and trauma that you've experienced.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Had to undergo.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I really, it would be very easy to take that grief and just completely retreat from public life.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I think what you've done is really a model for how all of us that experience loss can channel that grief into something positive.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And you're really inspiring.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I'm grateful that you've chosen to channel that grief into activism.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I have three brief questions for you, and then I'll look forward to hearing from you, sir.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So you told us in your testimony about a gold star mother who wanted to be here but couldn't leave her home because she lacks the mobility equipment and assistance she needs, and that's just heartbreaking, and I'd like our committee to do more than simply acknowledge it.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: With her permission, I hope that you'll be willing to

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: to connect her with my office so that we can work with the appropriate agencies to identify what assistance might be available, and I'm happy to go to wherever she is.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I'm wondering if this is a problem you're encountering with other military families as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Yes, she's not the only one.

chapters.summary: Nelson defines Silver Star families as family members of veterans who served, were injured, or have mental health issues. She identifies three roundtable priorities: awareness and education, communication and language, and ensuring families know their designation. She shares an anecdote of a woman who didn't know she was a White Star family member.
chapters.title: Nelson explains Silver Star families and identifies three roundtable priorities

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: You suggested, and I think it's a great idea, you suggested convening a roundtable with white star families to hear directly about their needs.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'd certainly be interested in doing that.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: If we organized a roundtable through this committee, what are the three most pressing issues you'd want us to address?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And would you be willing to help us bring those families together?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Yes, and I would believe to bring together also Silver Star because not too many people know what a Silver Star family is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Do anybody know what a Silver Star family is?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I only know through, because I've heard you speak on this before, but why don't you tell the public?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Shall I?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So Silver Star Family Member is a family member of a veteran that served our country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Whether they was injured, have mental health issues, or even work in everyday jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Like our family at DVS, that is a Silver Star family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Their families are considered Silver Star.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Gold Star are families like me, our veterans who died by suicide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: But that definition changes because...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This particular Gold Star mom's son, Pat,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: in a different way, but they still labeled her as Gold Star.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: White Star, we obviously know what that is because we're speaking about it today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And before I was speaking about it, no one knew a word about what it was.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And it was heartbreaking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And to finally...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Be able to be present here to speak about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: It's a big thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And the three points I think we would focus on is awareness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Awareness meaning education around it, acknowledging it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And I do believe the communities don't know that they are a silver star.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: The communities don't know that they are white star.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I was at something with CEC and there was a, oh, she was,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: in her 50s, and we was having conversations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I was telling her what I do, and she said, oh, I didn't know I was a white star.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: My father actually died by suicide because he couldn't take no more after he served our country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So, and those are the things that I feel in the communication and the language and how they speak with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: That's a third one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I could give you a list of more, but those three points.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Sure.

chapters.summary: Morano asks what a meaningful accountability system would look like for organizations serving military families. Nelson recommends undercover testing of organizations, truly anonymous complaint procedures that protect identities from retaliation, and ensuring organizations never learn who filed complaints.
chapters.title: Morano Q&A with Nelson: accountability systems for service organizations

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Well, we'll stay in touch.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And my last question, you spoke about experiencing disrespect within an organization that was supposed to support military families, and you recommended stronger complaint

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: procedures and independent evaluation without asking you to identify the organization.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: or revisit a difficult experience, what would a meaningful accountability system look like?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Should organizations receiving city funding be required to have a confidential complaint process or report complaints to DVS and demonstrate how to resolve them?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Do you have any other suggestions about how we can handle that going forward?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Yes, I do believe it's something you said that I've actually spoken about prior to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Going undercover into these organizations and companies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And I've spoken to DVS about this and telling, they don't have to know your real story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: You could just come as if you're looking for service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: You can just come and put in a whole acting moment as if you're even a gold star and see how people treat you, see how they communicate with you, see what services that they provide for you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And also I do feel that there should be a space where you can create a complaint.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Normally when you say complaint,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: anonymous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: It's not really anonymous if you think about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: I'm being honest with you because they'll still find out who you are.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Like when you call 911 and they're still going to know that you was the one who called.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: So in my eyes, it will never be anonymous, but it has to make sure that their information is protected and that that organization will never know who made it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: Because what happens is some people will come out and take repercussions behind it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: And if they have all your information and you know who you are, you will be harassed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mecca Nelson
utterances.text: This happens a lot.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Nelson.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Passaro.

chapters.summary: Passaro shares the story of his son Adam, a combat veteran who served in Army intelligence, later worked for Homeland Security, and died by suicide despite being in therapy. He describes Adam's PTSD, survivor guilt after his army buddy was killed, and credits Dr. Nelson with helping him through grief. He expresses gratitude for the White Star Family Day resolution.
chapters.title: Anthony Passaro testimony: son Adam's military service, PTSD, and suicide

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thanks for being here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And I just want to thank this council for recognizing Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: Megan Nelson today and myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And it's just amazing the work that she's doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: When you said she was a role model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: She's a role model to her daughter, who was three years old at the time, and how she brought her up with the values.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: She never turned to drugs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: She never, you know, this could happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: You lose your father, and, you know, you get bitter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: But she didn't make that happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: You know, she stood on top of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: She's one of the reasons I'm here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: Because I was a goner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: You know, you lose your son.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: It's a tragedy, you know, because he was going for therapy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And one of the mornings...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: He was in therapy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: That afternoon, he took his own life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And he suffered from PTSD, and he suffered from survivor guilt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: His army buddy got killed in front of him, and he took it very bad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And he had that guy's dog tags tattooed on his own arm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: That's how much it affected him, you know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: But he persevered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And he, you know, he was a sergeant and he went from human resources type of thing in the Army to intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And so when he had to leave the Army because of PTSD and he had gotten injured,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: Homeland Security scooped him up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And he did really, really well with them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: So everything was going wonderful, you know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: And then he actually did a really great thing with Homeland Security, and he got a big award.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: We all had to go to Washington.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
utterances.text: So, but anyway, if it wasn't for Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Passaro
